topics: cabe destacar que: señalar un dato importante

stories.title: Memoria y justicia
stories.summary: A closing look at how these countries tried, imperfectly and unevenly, to reckon with what had happened -- through trials, amnesty laws, their later reversal, and memory sites built on the ruins of former detention centers.
topics: a día de hoy: hablar de la situación actual

stories.title: ¿Qué es una revolución?
stories.summary: Not every change of government is a revolution -- a look at what actually separates a palace coup from the kind of upheaval that rewrites who owns what and who has power.
topics: no es lo mismo... que: distinciones conceptuales

stories.title: Tierra y poder
stories.summary: Nearly every genuine revolutionary movement in the region's history traces back to the same grievance: who owns the land, and who was pushed off it to get there.
topics: conectores causales: debido a que, a causa de que

stories.title: Trabajadores y movimientos sociales
stories.summary: The countryside wasn't the only source of revolutionary pressure -- a second, urban current, carried by immigrant organizers and industrial workers, was building at the same time.
topics: sin que + subjuntivo: lo que no llegó a ocurrir

stories.title: Revolución y Estado
stories.summary: Winning a revolution turns out to be the easier half of the problem -- what comes after, building a state that can actually govern, is where most revolutionary movements have historically struggled hardest.
topics: futuro simple: predicciones sobre lo que vendrá

stories.title: Cuando cambia el orden
stories.summary: A closing theory of revolution: pulling together land, class, immigration-fed labor organizing, and state-building into one general picture of when the old order actually breaks.

stories.title: Cuba antes de 1959
stories.summary: Lejos de ser un país pobre y aislado, pre-revolutionary Cuba had one of Latin America's higher per-capita incomes -- and one of its most unequal, US-dominated economies.
topics: lejos de + infinitivo: corregir una idea equivocada

stories.title: Fidel Castro y la revolución
stories.summary: A failed attack on an army barracks, a shipwrecked landing, and two years hiding in the mountains -- an unlikely sequence that acabó por overthrowing a government backed by the United States.
topics: acabar por + infinitivo: cómo terminó un proceso

stories.title: Una revolución socialista
stories.summary: It didn't start out calling itself socialist -- but month by month, the new government moved cada vez más toward Moscow and cada vez menos toward Washington.
topics: cada vez menos... cada vez más: describir una radicalización

stories.title: Bahía de Cochinos y misiles
stories.summary: In the space of eighteen months, Cuba went from a failed CIA-backed invasion to the single closest moment the entire world has ever come to nuclear war.
topics: a punto de + infinitivo: al borde de que algo ocurra

stories.title: Cuba y América Latina
stories.summary: A closing look at what Cuba meant for the rest of the region -- a genuine inspiration to some, an existential threat to others, and, either way, impossible to ignore for the following three decades.
topics: no por... deja de: matizar sin negar del todo

stories.title: Una isla en plena Guerra Fría
El Porfiriato
stories.summary: By 1910, Porfirio Díaz had been running Mexico for thirty-four years under the slogan "order and progress" -- and that very durability was quietly building the pressure that would finally break it.
topics: llevar + gerundio: cuánto tiempo llevaba ocurriendo algo

stories.title: Madero y la revolución
stories.summary: An unlikely revolutionary -- a wealthy landowner's son -- issued the call to arms that actually got Díaz to resign after 34 years.
topics: subjuntivo tras verbos de petición: pedir que, exigir que

stories.title: Zapata y Villa
stories.summary: Two revolutionaries, two very different revolutions -- a southern peasant leader fighting purely for land, and a northern cavalry commander fighting for something less clearly defined.
topics: el hecho de que + subjuntivo: nominalizar una idea

stories.title: La Constitución de 1917
stories.summary: Out of years of chaotic fighting came one of the most radical constitutions of its era -- a document that put land reform and labor rights directly into the country's fundamental law.

stories.title: El legado revolucionario
stories.summary: A closing look at what the Mexican Revolution actually produced -- not so much a finished transformation as a single party that governed, in the revolution's name, for the rest of the century.
topics: no tanto... como: matizar una comparación

stories.title: El imperio español
stories.summary: How Spain actually governed an empire across an ocean months away: viceroyalties that kept splitting, a trade monopoly run from one city, and a legal loophole that let colonial officials quietly ignore royal orders.

stories.title: Una sociedad jerárquica
stories.summary: How the colonial hierarchy was written directly into law: two parallel legal systems, genealogical paperwork required for university or guild membership, and a grievance that quietly built for three centuries.

stories.title: La Iglesia
stories.summary: The Church as the colony's real infrastructure: universities founded within decades of the conquest, self-governing Jesuit mission-states with their own orchestras, and an Inquisition that explicitly could not prosecute indigenous people.

stories.title: La vida cotidiana
stories.summary: How colonial cities were literally designed by royal decree, how daily life in the markets blurred the legal separation between 'two republics', and the bishop who banned chocolate in church — and reportedly paid for it with his life.

stories.title: Vivir en la colonia
stories.summary: Nearly three centuries under one system — longer than most of these countries have since existed as independent states — and what actually held it together day to day.
topics: voz pasiva: síntesis de la sociedad colonial

stories.title: La Sagrada Família: cien años de construcción
stories.summary: Adapted and simplified from the Wikipedia article on Barcelona's Sagrada Família basilica, for A2 learners.
